Found it in `src/agentic_hil/tools.py`, in `flash_firmware` (lines 274-310):

```python
image_path = payload.get("image_path")
artifact_id = payload.get("artifact_id")
if bool(image_path) == bool(artifact_id):
    return tool_error("flash_firmware", "invalid_argument", "Provide exactly one of image_path or artifact_id.")
```

When both `image_path` and `artifact_id` are present (both truthy), `bool(image_path) == bool(artifact_id)` evaluates to `True == True`, so the method short-circuits and returns a `tool_error` with `error_type` `"invalid_argument"` and the message `"Provide exactly one of image_path or artifact_id."` — it never proceeds to permission checks for `reset_after_flash`, artifact validation/staging, or the actual `self.backend.flash_firmware(...)` call. (Note: the same check also rejects the case where neither is provided, since `False == False` is also `True`.)
